title: F0 rejection audit: unvoiced frames versus missed voicing
hypothesis: Most frames rejected as no_candidate are aperiodic (fricatives, closures, breath) or too weak to carry a period; a minority sit inside voiced spans and show harmonic-comb evidence, and those are a candidate-model miss rather than a threshold problem. Loosening the CMND gate is therefore not the fix, and any change must be justified by comb/cepstrum evidence per frame.

notes: Diagnostic only: track_pitch thresholds untouched (CMND gate 0.55, fmax 900 Hz), no frame interpolated. 2052 frames / 12 utterances / 12 speakers from the AISHELL-3 test split. 281 no_candidate frames decompose into 174 aperiodic, 103 boundary_or_weak and 4 suspected_miss; zero suspected_miss frames sit between two accepted frames. SSB04350040 (250.0 vs 280.3 Hz) is explained by a minority of legacy octave/sub-octave jumps: median per-frame offset 5.4 cents but 18.2% of frames differ by more than 50 cents, and independent HPS/cepstrum estimates agree with the viterbi tracker on those frames. v1 (uncalibrated fixed thresholds) is preserved as a counter-example. No listening test.
